practice: Checks written from real failures, 20 to 50 to start
how: Every 'change:' comment you write becomes a check in the build gate. The gate list starts small and grows from real review comments, never from a rubric.

practice: Layered checks: automated, then a human spot read, then a deeper pass
how: Gate G3 and G4 run in the agent, you read every post (G5), and one row a week gets a full walk with FE (G7).

practice: Review on the artifact: a preview link with comments on by default
how: Every run ends in a Vercel preview that opens where Sam starts. Comment there or in ClickUp; no review meeting.

practice: Validate the agent's change before a human sees it
how: typecheck, tests, biome, copy lint, token diff and screenshot baselines run before the Slack post exists.

practice: Separate shipping code from releasing a feature
how: Locked commits live on design/v3 behind the design-preview build flag, so FE pulls them on its own cadence.

practice: Design engineering: the same person sketches, gets feedback and ships
how: The agent designs in code and in Figma in the same run; the prototype is the handoff, Figma is the record.

practice: Quality is the named metric, defended by small teams and a one-week fix promise
how: No count of deliveries is a KPI here. A 'change:' comment jumps the queue at the next run, within hours not weeks.

practice: Short one-owner briefs, issues not user stories
how: The ClickUp task is the brief: job, goal, telemetry, deliverables, agent brief. Nothing else.

practice: The tracker is the only source of truth for status
how: ClickUp status is the queue. A row is WIP only when its task says in progress; the sheet reads it, never the other way round.

practice: Named crit formats, including an FYI lane that asks for nothing
how: Three post kinds: 'Review ready' needs a verdict, 'FYI' is a rainy-state add or a token change, 'Question' blocks a row until you answer.

practice: Catch drift where the source changes
how: Every kit component maps to its console component; a frame using an unmapped component fails the Figma gate.

practice: Three-section spec: problem, solution with alternatives, rollout with success criteria
how: Each row reads the same way: job (problem), directions and pick (solution), goal and telemetry (success).

practice: The same named phases every time, with a visible sign-off
how: 13 stops and 8 gates above; 'where is this' is always a status in ClickUp and a gate in the sheet.

practice: Job stories over personas: situation, motivation, outcome
how: Sam appears only in job text: Job, Situation, Sam wants to, So that. Rainy paths are the emotional and social criteria.

practice: One north star plus a few movable inputs; no vanity or lagging counts
how: FPR is the north star, TTFA and TTFDA are the inputs. Designs delivered per day is never reported as a KPI.

practice: The tracking plan is a reviewable artifact with its own sign-off
how: Gate G2: every event on the row has an owner and a status before the row goes to review.

practice: Ship, show, ask: not every change needs the same gate
how: Ship: copy and token fixes inside a row's scope. Show: extra rainy states, posted FYI. Ask: anything touching a locked design or new scope.

practice: A fixed betting moment with an appetite instead of an estimate
how: The four runs are the cadence; the days budget on the row is the appetite; your pick in ClickUp is the bet.

practice: Never auto-merge agent output; make it easy to validate, attribute and reject
how: The agent never sets Done. One row, one commit, one Figma section, so a rejection costs one row.

practice: Status posts state the outcome, not the activity, and name what unblocks
how: The post format above: done and pending your review, links first, rainy states covered, open questions with who answers them.
